recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-26684 unless the work group later wants a purely editorial cleanup of the long Questionnaire.item.required comment.
issue_request: FHIR-26684 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Questionnaire and asked to clarify Questionnaire.item.required: remove the vague 'generally assumed' default wording, explain required group behavior, and state that child required items only matter when their parent item is present in the QuestionnaireResponse.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites git commit 3d82dea189a1065b0bba9be644260a7b4e2ae9cc. That commit changed source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml by replacing the meaningWhenMissing text with 'Items are assumed not to be required unless explicitly specified, though extensions may impose additional expectations' and adding parent-present/non-required-group guidance to the Questionnaire.item.required comment.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in source/fhir.ini. Later same-element Published/Persuasive clarifications FHIR-29311 and FHIR-32151 preserved and refined the required guidance; FHIR-32151 added the current direct-answer and answered-descendant wording. FHIR SDC minutes list FHIR-26684 as Persuasive, and relevant Questionnaire Zulip threads support the same contextual interpretation of required.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative StructureDefinition source already states that missing required means not required unless explicitly specified, required groups need an answered descendant question, required descendants only matter when their parent is present, and required containers do not automatically make descendants required.
